problem: Given the hyperboloid of one sheet $(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{9}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$

feedback.problem: Given the hyperboloid of two sheets $\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}-(z+2)^{2}=-1,$ find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}-(z+2)^{2} & =-1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}+1 & =(z+2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(z+2)^{2} & =\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}+1 \\ z+2 & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}+1} \\ z & =-2\pm \sqrt{\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

The square root is defined only for non-negative arguments. However, notice that for all $(x,y)\in {R}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}+1\ge 0.
$$

Therefore, the domain of $z(x,y)$ is ${R}^{2}.$
